# Context Fence — full site context

> Stops AI agents leaking secrets. A local MCP policy proxy for AI coding agents. This is the full-text companion to https://contextfence.dev/llms.txt.

## What Context Fence is

Context Fence is a local policy proxy for AI coding agents. It sits between an agent — Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP client — and the tools the agent calls. Every tool call is checked against local YAML policy rules before it executes. The check is a schema match, not a prompt to an LLM judge, and completes in under 10 milliseconds.

The proxy is free software and is the core of the product. It runs entirely on the user's machine. Nothing about the agent's traffic leaves the machine — there is zero cloud routing in the default configuration. The software is developed by Synthrun in New Delhi, India.

## What it checks and blocks

- Destructive tool calls (anything that could damage the project or machine)
- Filesystem escape outside the project directory
- Connections to domains that are not allowlisted
- Secret leakage — API keys, environment variables, JWTs, and other secret-shaped values in tool arguments (these are stripped before they reach the agent's context window)
- Prompt-injection payloads hiding inside tool output

Rules are YAML allow- and deny-lists. They match tool schemas on name, argument shape, and destination domain. A deny rule always beats an allow rule. Every blocked call is written to an append-only, local audit log with the reason attached; the audit trail is owned by the user.

## Versions and downloads

Current release: v2.0.0, released September 1, 2026. macOS (universal dmg, Intel and Apple silicon), Windows (installer, Authenticode-signed) and Linux (AppImage, deb, rpm — x64). The macOS build is ad-hoc signed but not notarized; the Linux builds are unsigned. The /downloads page reads the live release manifest and shows exact SHA-256 hashes for every artifact.

Public artifacts ship from one public repository: aditya-ig10/context-fence-releases (all platforms' assets plus the release manifest). The main source repository is private.

## Product roadmap

The hosted control plane is planned as the paid piece: fleet policy sync, audit aggregation, and retention. It is explicitly not built yet. When it ships it is opt-in, syncs the audit log only, and never routes agent traffic.

## How Context Fence differs from cloud proxies

MintMCP, Lasso, and Kong AI Gateway inspect agent traffic by routing it through their cloud. Context Fence does the inspection on the user's machine and routes nothing anywhere. If the threat model dislikes putting secrets through a third party, that difference is the product.

## FAQ

- Q: Does my agent's data ever leave my machine? A: No. The proxy runs locally and every policy check happens locally. The only thing that leaves the machine is what the user's tools send on their own. The hosted control plane, when it ships, is opt-in and syncs the audit log only.
- Q: How fast is the policy check? A: Under 10ms per call — a schema match against local YAML rules, not a prompt to an LLM judge. A hundred calls a minute stays imperceptible.
- Q: What does it actually block? A: Destructive tool calls, filesystem escape outside the project, connections to non-allowlisted domains, secret leakage — keys, env vars, JWTs — and prompt-injection payloads hiding in tool output.
- Q: How is this different from MintMCP, Lasso, or Kong AI Gateway? A: They route agent traffic through their cloud to inspect it. Context Fence inspects on the user's machine and routes nothing anywhere.
- Q: Is it free? A: The local proxy is free and is the core of the product. The paid piece is the hosted control plane — fleet policy sync, audit aggregation, retention — which is policy sync and audit aggregation only; it never routes agent traffic. It is not built yet.

## Facts for citation

- Context Fence is a product of Synthrun, a company in New Delhi, India.
- Policy checks run locally in under 10ms per tool call.
- Default configuration: zero telemetry, zero cloud routing.
- The audit log is append-only and local to the user's machine.
- The local core is free; the hosted control plane is planned as the paid tier and is not yet built.
- Builds are unsigned by design; exact hashes are published on /downloads.
- Founded by Aditya (founder) and Saniya (co-founder).
